videos.title: AI Stocks Are Cracking. Spending Is Outrunning Wages. What Happens When the Wealth Effect Fades?
videos.description:
Bob Elliott and Aahan Menon examine how stock-market wealth is helping consumers spend faster than their paychecks grow—and what that means for corporate profits if stocks stop rising.

Elliott, co-founder of Unlimited, and Menon, founder of Prometheus Research, join Matt Zeigler to connect household spending, AI investment, and the earnings expectations built into markets. They discuss where their growth outlooks differ, why persistent inflation complicates the Fed's choices, and how bonds can look attractive against stocks while still looking unattractive against cash.

The conversation also explores whether AI is producing the economy-wide gains needed to justify its investment boom, how forward spending commitments could reverse, and why both guests distinguish those risks from a repeat of the 2008 credit crisis.

Topics covered:
- What the midterm election could change for fiscal policy and data-center construction
- Oil and AI as the competing forces behind inflation and growth expectations
- Bob Elliott's distinction between peak growth and peak pricing of growth
- How household wealth and drawing down savings support consumer spending
- Aahan Menon on wages, workforce participation, immigration, and demographics
- Why both guests think central banks are reluctant to deliver tighter policy
- Bonds versus stocks, bonds versus cash, and Aahan Menon's inflation-nowcast rule
- Bob Elliott's test for AI: accelerating productivity and revenue beyond the technology sector
- H
